chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Rifah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the divorced woman when she is menstruating, does her husband have the right to take her back (raj'ah)? He said, 'Yes, until she becomes pure.' Because in this report there is no indication that he has the right to take her back until she becomes pure from the third menstruation, and if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it to mean that he possesses the right of revocation during menstruation if it is the first or second.
ai.seo_question: Can a husband take back his divorced wife while she is menstruating during the revocable waiting period?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the juristic principle of 'takhyir' (interpretive flexibility) is applied to reconcile the literal text with the broader legal framework, confirming that the husband's right of revocation extends through the entire menstrual period for the first and second divorces. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of deriving specific rulings from general statements by examining the absence of restrictive conditions in the primary text.
